descriptionChirho: Quantitative sense indicating a large number of persons, things, or occurrences. Used frequently in Acts of many days, many people, and many believers (e.g., Luke 8:32, 23:9; Acts 9:23,43, 12:12, 14:21, 18:18, 19:19, 20:8, 27:7; Rom 15:23; 1 Cor 11:30). Rendered Arabic كثير, Hebrew רַבִּים, Hindi बहुत, Korean 많은, Spanish muchos.

Indicating large extent, degree, size, or duration of time, used adjectivally of periods (a considerable time), crowds (a considerable crowd), intensity (great light, great commotion). Frequent in Luke-Acts for temporal and intensive uses (Luke 7:12, 8:27, 20:9, 23:8; Acts 8:11, 11:24,26, 14:3, 19:26, 20:11,37, 22:6, 27:9; Mark 10:46; Matt 28:12). Rendered Arabic كثير/كافي, Hebrew רַב, Korean 큰/오랜, Spanish considerable/bastante.

Of persons who are qualified, deserving, capable, or competent enough for a role, task, or honor. Used of John the Baptist declaring himself unworthy to carry Jesus' sandals (Matt 3:11; Mark 1:7; Luke 3:16), the centurion feeling unworthy for Jesus to enter his house (Matt 8:8; Luke 7:6), Paul as not fit to be called an apostle (1 Cor 15:9), sufficiency from God (2 Cor 2:16, 3:5), and faithful men competent to teach (2 Tim 2:2). Rendered Arabic أهل/كافين, Hebrew רָאוּי, Hindi योग्य, Korean 합당한, Spanish digno/capaz.

Adequate or satisfactory in quantity or degree to meet a need, often used substantively or predicatively to mean 'it is enough.' Used of giving Pilate satisfaction (Mark 15:15), Jesus saying 'It is enough' about the swords (Luke 22:38), and the punishment being sufficient (2 Cor 2:6). Rendered Arabic كافٍ, Hebrew דַּי/מַסְפִּיק, Hindi पर्याप्त, Korean 충분하다, Spanish suficiente.

Substantivized legal/technical term (τὸ ἱκανόν) referring to a financial guarantee, bail, or security bond posted before civil authorities to ensure compliance or appearance. Used in Acts 17:9 where Jason and others posted bond before the city officials at Thessalonica. Rendered Arabic كفالة, Hebrew הָעֵרָבוֹן, Hindi ज़मानत, Korean 보증금, Spanish fianza.
